#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-asserting harness for the memsize demo.
#
# This IS the "test framework" for these demos: a program's pass/fail is its
# SimControl exit code + stdout marker, and the driver's pass/fail is its own
# process exit code. Both are asserted here in portable bash -- no gtest, no
# libstdc++ on the target, nothing to cross-compile. Same pattern as andesim's
# own tests/andes_sim/*.sh.
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
ENG=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}
SUM='0x5e949e00'          # checksum is --mem-size-independent (determinism)

pass=0 fail=0
# assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD...
assert() {
  local desc=$1 want_rc=$2 want_re=$3; shift 3
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] && grep -qiE "$want_re" <<<"$out"; then
    printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$desc"; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] %s\n       rc=%s (want %s), no /%s/ in:\n       %s\n' \
      "$desc" "$rc" "$want_rc" "$want_re" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

echo "--- accept + run (checksum is the same at any size) ---"
assert "fast  64M  runs, checksum $SUM"  0 "memsize PASS checksum=$SUM" \
  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size 64M  memsize.elf
assert "fast  256M runs, same checksum"  0 "memsize PASS checksum=$SUM" \
  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size 256M memsize.elf

echo "--- different sizes: hybrid DRAM window tracks --mem-size ---"
assert "hybrid 1.5G   -> DRAM 1536M"      0 "DRAM.*1536M" \
  "$A" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 1.5G   memsize.elf
assert "hybrid 131072K-> DRAM 128M"       0 "DRAM.*128M" \
  "$A" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 131072K memsize.elf

echo "--- boundary: cap = 2 GiB - one V-scratch page ---"
assert "hybrid 2047M accepted (largest)"  0 "2047M" \
  "$A" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 2047M memsize.elf
assert "hybrid 2G rejected (overflow)"    2 "exceeds the AE350 DRAM window" \
  "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 2G memsize.elf

echo "--- negative: invalid specs rejected before any spawn ---"
assert "0   -> must be > 0"                2 "must be > 0" \
  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size 0   memsize.elf
assert "-5  -> expected <number>"          2 "expected <number>" \
  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size -5  memsize.elf
assert "abc -> expected <number>"          2 "expected <number>" \
  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size abc memsize.elf
assert "fast 1000 -> whole MiB rule"       2 "whole MiB" \
  "$A" run --mode fast --mem-size 1000 memsize.elf

echo "--- fit: --mem-size vs the program's own 64 MiB static footprint ---"
assert "big ELF @ 32M rejected"            2 "raise --mem-size" \
  "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 32M memsize_big.elf
assert "big ELF @ 128M fits DRAM"          0 "fits DRAM" \
  "$A" run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 128M memsize_big.elf

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-asserting harness for the cache demo: the transported cache-enable
# state must be worth a multiple in the hybrid cycle figure. Same pattern as
# demo/memsize/check.sh.
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
ENG=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}
RATIO_MIN=${RATIO_MIN:-2}   # uncached must cost > RATIO_MIN x cached

pass=0 fail=0
# assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD...
assert() {
  local desc=$1 want_rc=$2 want_re=$3; shift 3
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] && grep -qiE "$want_re" <<<"$out"; then
    printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$desc"; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] %s\n       rc=%s (want %s), no /%s/ in:\n       %s\n' \
      "$desc" "$rc" "$want_rc" "$want_re" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

# run_cycles CMD... -> echoes the N of "[andesim] N cycles", empty on failure
run_cycles() {
  local out
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1) || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; return 1; }
  sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1
}

echo "--- both builds are functionally sound (fast; QEMU has no caches) ---"
assert "fast cache_on:  CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_on.elf
assert "fast cache_off: CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_off.elf

echo "--- the same ROI, hybrid, cached vs uncached ---"
on=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_on.elf)
off=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_off.elf)

if [ -z "$on" ] || [ -z "$off" ]; then
  echo "[FAIL] hybrid figure missing (on='$on' off='$off')"; fail=$((fail+1))
else
  ratio=$(awk -v a="$off" -v b="$on" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", a/b}')
  printf 'cached   (crt0 enable transported): %8s cycles\n' "$on"
  printf 'uncached (program cleared IC|DC):   %8s cycles\n' "$off"
  printf 'ratio: %sx (must be > %sx)\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
  if [ "$off" -gt $((RATIO_MIN * on)) ]; then
    printf '[PASS] cache-enable transport is worth %sx on this kernel\n' "$ratio"
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] uncached/cached ratio %sx did not clear %sx\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

# run_cycles CMD... -> echoes the N of "[andesim] N cycles", empty on failure
run_cycles() {
  local out
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1) || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; return 1; }
  sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1
}

echo "--- both builds are functionally sound (fast; QEMU has no caches) ---"
assert "fast cache_on:  CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_on.elf
assert "fast cache_off: CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_off.elf

echo "--- the same ROI, hybrid, cached vs uncached ---"
on=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_on.elf)
off=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_off.elf)

if [ -z "$on" ] || [ -z "$off" ]; then
  echo "[FAIL] hybrid figure missing (on='$on' off='$off')"; fail=$((fail+1))
else
  ratio=$(awk -v a="$off" -v b="$on" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", a/b}')
  printf 'cached   (crt0 enable transported): %8s cycles\n' "$on"
  printf 'uncached (program cleared IC|DC):   %8s cycles\n' "$off"
  printf 'ratio: %sx (must be > %sx)\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
  if [ "$off" -gt $((RATIO_MIN * on)) ]; then
    printf '[PASS] cache-enable transport is worth %sx on this kernel\n' "$ratio"
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] uncached/cached ratio %sx did not clear %sx\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-rvv
make run-fp
make run-syscall
make run-coremark
make run-dhrystone
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `fp-*`, `syscall-*`, `coremark-*`
and `dhrystone-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/rvv` tests the vector unit: the ROI runs an RVV-intrinsic kernel
(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works); the
workload is an 8x8x8 int32 GEMM. The QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar
reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector unit and
compares. `RVV_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after the
handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

`demo/fp` covers the scalar FPU's state, `fcsr`, the way `demo/rvv`
covers the vector unit. The QEMU phase clears `fflags`, sets the
rounding mode to RTZ (the reset default is RNE) and raises the sticky
divide-by-zero flag with a real `1.0f/0.0f`; the vsim ROI computes
`1.0f/3.0f` -- a quotient that rounds DIFFERENTLY under RTZ
(`0x3eaaaaaa`) and RNE (`0x3eaaaaab`) -- then reads the CSRs back.
`FP_OK` means the transported `frm` steered a real divide after the
handoff (not just a CSR readback), the pre-handoff DZ flag is still
sticky, and the divide's own NX landed on top of it: `fcsr` crossed
intact.

`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
main's return value through SimControl).

`demo/coremark` runs a real benchmark, EEMBC CoreMark, with the EEMBC
sources untouched: the ROI markers live in the port layer
(`core_portme.c`), inside `start_time()` and `stop_time()` -- the two
functions that already delimit the timed run -- so the hybrid window is
exactly the region CoreMark times itself with its own `mcycle` reads.
That makes the modes cross-check each other: cycle mode's self-reported
`Total ticks` and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region and agree within ~0.5% (the hybrid window starts with cold
caches and includes the marker/call boundary). The pc-trigger variant
gets the same window from the symbols alone
(`--pc-start start_time --pc-end stop_time`). On hybrid the run ends at
`stop_time()`'s exit marker, so CoreMark's report (CRCs, validation)
prints on fast and cycle only; the hybrid output is just the cycle
figure. `ITERATIONS=1` by default -- the CRCs still validate, and each
extra iteration adds RTL simulation time.

`demo/dhrystone` applies the same recipe to Dhrystone 2.2a (the vsim
port, which times with `mcycle`/`minstret` instead of UNIX time APIs):
the counter reads moved into `start_time()`/`stop_time()`, which carry
the ROI markers outside the reads and double as the
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbols. The guest's self-reported `CycleCnt`
(cycle mode) and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region; on hybrid the run ends at `stop_time()`'s marker, so the
`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
second pass with `-DPASS2`).

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/rvv/       RVV-intrinsic kernel (8x8x8 GEMM) inside the ROI
demo/fp/        scalar FP state: frm steers a divide in the ROI, fflags stay sticky
demo/syscall/   stdio, host file io and exit code on every mode
demo/coremark/  EEMBC CoreMark; the ROI is the benchmark's own timed region
demo/dhrystone/ Dhrystone 2.2a; same recipe, two-pass compile kept
```

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-rvv
make run-fp
make run-cache
make run-syscall
make run-coremark
make run-dhrystone
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `fp-*`, `cache-*`, `syscall-*`,
`coremark-*` and `dhrystone-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/rvv` tests the vector unit: the ROI runs an RVV-intrinsic kernel
(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works); the
workload is an 8x8x8 int32 GEMM. The QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar
reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector unit and
compares. `RVV_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after the
handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

`demo/fp` covers the scalar FPU's state, `fcsr`, the way `demo/rvv`
covers the vector unit. The QEMU phase clears `fflags`, sets the
rounding mode to RTZ (the reset default is RNE) and raises the sticky
divide-by-zero flag with a real `1.0f/0.0f`; the vsim ROI computes
`1.0f/3.0f` -- a quotient that rounds DIFFERENTLY under RTZ
(`0x3eaaaaaa`) and RNE (`0x3eaaaaab`) -- then reads the CSRs back.
`FP_OK` means the transported `frm` steered a real divide after the
handoff (not just a CSR readback), the pre-handoff DZ flag is still
sticky, and the divide's own NX landed on top of it: `fcsr` crossed
intact.

`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
main's return value through SimControl).

`demo/coremark` runs a real benchmark, EEMBC CoreMark, with the EEMBC
sources untouched: the ROI markers live in the port layer
(`core_portme.c`), inside `start_time()` and `stop_time()` -- the two
functions that already delimit the timed run -- so the hybrid window is
exactly the region CoreMark times itself with its own `mcycle` reads.
That makes the modes cross-check each other: cycle mode's self-reported
`Total ticks` and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region and agree within ~0.5% (the hybrid window starts with cold
caches and includes the marker/call boundary). The pc-trigger variant
gets the same window from the symbols alone
(`--pc-start start_time --pc-end stop_time`). On hybrid the run ends at
`stop_time()`'s exit marker, so CoreMark's report (CRCs, validation)
prints on fast and cycle only; the hybrid output is just the cycle
figure. `ITERATIONS=1` by default -- the CRCs still validate, and each
extra iteration adds RTL simulation time.

`demo/dhrystone` applies the same recipe to Dhrystone 2.2a (the vsim
port, which times with `mcycle`/`minstret` instead of UNIX time APIs):
the counter reads moved into `start_time()`/`stop_time()`, which carry
the ROI markers outside the reads and double as the
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbols. The guest's self-reported `CycleCnt`
(cycle mode) and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region; on hybrid the run ends at `stop_time()`'s marker, so the
`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
second pass with `-DPASS2`).

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/rvv/       RVV-intrinsic kernel (8x8x8 GEMM) inside the ROI
demo/fp/        scalar FP state: frm steers a divide in the ROI, fflags stay sticky
demo/syscall/   stdio, host file io and exit code on every mode
demo/coremark/  EEMBC CoreMark; the ROI is the benchmark's own timed region
demo/dhrystone/ Dhrystone 2.2a; same recipe, two-pass compile kept
```

# andesim-demo test roadmap

Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.

Conventions (same as the existing demos):

- Layout: `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; host-side checks go
  in `demo/<name>/check.sh` (the `memsize` precedent).
- Top-level `Makefile` gets `run-<name>` and the per-mode targets; `README.md`
  gets a short section describing what the demo proves.
- Pass signal: either the guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI, or
  `check.sh` asserts on the driver's output. Every demo must fail loudly.
- Demos run on every mode where the feature exists (some are hybrid-only or
  fast-only; each entry says which).

Priority = file order. 1-3 are headline USER_GUIDE features with zero demo
coverage today.

---

## 1. hotloops

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (pc trigger); the detector itself runs fast.

Measure a binary you cannot edit. `main.c` has one known hot loop (a
checksum over an array, >=10 iterations) and NO ROI markers. `check.sh`
runs `$(ANDESIM)/build/hotloops --min-iters 10 <elf>`, asserts the report
names the hot function, extracts the ready `measure:` line (a
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair), and pastes it into
`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`. Closed loop: the detector's
output feeds the measurement command with no human guessing.

- Key files: `demo/hotloops/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh sees the hot function in the hotloops report AND a
  `[andesim] N cycles` line from the hybrid run using the reported PCs.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 4.3, docs/hotloops.md.

## 2. verify

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid only (marker trigger).

Trust the figure. A state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP math, an RVV
loop, CSR writes) runs with `--verify`: andesim re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU
up to the ROI exit and compares the drained state field by field against
the cycle engine.

- Key files: `demo/verify/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: output contains `[state-diff] PASS` and `[verify] PASS: vsim drain
  matches the QEMU oracle`.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.7.

## 3. kanata

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid only.

See the pipeline of exactly the ROI. A small kernel runs with
`--kanata roi.kanata --objdump kernel.S` (the dump generated at build time
with `objdump -d`). Users open the file in Konata; check.sh proves it is
well-formed without a GUI.

- Key files: `demo/kanata/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts the Kanata header line, that a known kernel
  mnemonic from the objdump is embedded, and the trace is non-trivial
  (more than a handful of retired instructions).
- Constraint to demo: marker mode needs exactly ONE exit marker in the ELF
  (more -> andesim errors and points at `--trigger pc`).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.8.

## 4. engines

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (optionally cycle too) on BOTH installed engines.

One binary, N cores - design-space exploration. The same kernel is measured
on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` and `vsim:ax46mpv_advanced`; check.sh parses both
cycle figures and prints a small comparison table.

- Key files: `demo/engines/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: both engines produce a `[andesim] N cycles` line; table printed.
- Deps: none. Requires both engines installed (skip with a clear message if
  `list engines` shows only one).

## 5. fp

State: DONE
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).

Scalar FP state transport - fills the coverage gap next to `rvv` (which is
integer-V only). The QEMU phase sets a non-default rounding mode (`frm` =
RTZ) and raises a sticky `fflags` bit; the vsim ROI computes a
rounding-mode-sensitive result and checks: the result matches
expected-for-RTZ, and the pre-ROI sticky flag is still set. Proves
`fcsr` (+ `mstatus.FS`) crossed the handoff.

- Key files: `demo/fp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest prints `FP_OK`.
- Deps: none.

## 6. cache

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (marker), two variants of one source.

Why timing-config transport matters. The same kernel is built twice from
one `main.c`: variant A keeps crt0's cache enable (transported
`mcache_ctl`), variant B writes `mcache_ctl = 0` before the ROI. check.sh
runs both hybrid measurements and asserts the uncached figure is much
larger. Doubles as a write-mask demo: the restore carries variant B's
disable only because the program itself wrote the CSR.

- Key files: `demo/cache/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(off) > 2 * cycles(on)` (calibrate the
  factor once real numbers exist).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE section 6 ("Config that matters for
  timing rides along").

## 7. roi_rules

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (marker + pc) vs cycle as the reference.

Trigger semantics and measurement hygiene, executable. A `noinline` kernel
is called 3 times; both triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is
the FIRST call only. check.sh asserts the hybrid figure is far below the
cycle-mode total (which contains all 3 calls + boot). The source shows the
hygiene rule from USER_GUIDE 4.2: anchor the kernel through memory inside
the marker span.

- Key files: `demo/roi_rules/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(hybrid) < cycles(cycle) / 3`.
- Deps: none.

## 8. diagnose

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (driver features, no new guest code needed - reuse the hello ELF).

The debugging workflow as a script. check.sh exercises, in order:
`--dry-run` (asserts 2 resolved command lines), `--print-memmap` (asserts
the DRAM/V-scratch rows), `--log-level 1` (asserts the `[andesim] mmap`
line), `--log-file` (asserts timestamped, level-tagged lines land in the
file), and one forced leg failure that must leave a repro bundle
(`[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at ...` -> assert `manifest.txt`
exists there). Open point for the build session: pick the most reliable
quick failure (candidate: a `--pc-end` that never retires, with a short
timeout).

- Key files: `demo/diagnose/{Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: every assertion in check.sh.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.5, 5.6, 5.10, 8.

## 9. rv32

State: TODO
Modes: fast only (no rv32 cycle engine installed; hybrid rejects rv32 by design).

The rv32 runtime flavor and engine auto-select. Build hello against
`build/runtime/rv32` (`-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d`), run `--mode fast` with
no `--engine`, and show the driver picked `qemu32` from the ELF width.

- Key files: `demo/rv32/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: hello output + exit code propagated; `--log-level 1` (or
  `--dry-run`) shows qemu32 was selected.
- Deps: needs an rv32-capable compiler (separate riscv32 gcc or multilib);
  the Makefile must skip with a clear message if the toolchain cannot do
  rv32.

## 10. gdb

State: TODO
Modes: fast first; cycle as a stretch goal.

Attach a debugger, scripted. fast: launch `--gdb` in the background, drive
`gdb-multiarch` in batch mode (`-ex 'target remote :1234'`, break at a
symbol, continue, print a variable, kill). cycle: needs `$ICEMAN` pointing
at an OpenOCD 0.12+ wrapper speaking remote_bitbang (the Andes-bundled
0.10 has a known bug against this DTM) - build only if the host has it.

- Key files: `demo/gdb/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: the gdb batch log shows the breakpoint hit and the expected
  variable value. check.sh skips (with a message) when gdb/OpenOCD are
  missing.
- Deps: none in-repo; host tools required. Build last.

## 11. priv

State: BLOCKED (engine not installed)
Modes: hybrid.

S/U-mode handoff: drop privilege before the ROI, prove the level and the
PMP mirror crossed. Requires the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired

`cache` is implemented, green, and committed (`f1dc453`). Measured on `ax45mpv_premium`: the same ROI costs **4,544 cycles cached vs 42,504 uncached — a 9.4x gap**, which is what the `mcache_ctl` transport is worth on this kernel.

How it works: `cache_on.elf` is the untouched program — crt0 enables the L1 caches at boot on QEMU, and only the transported CSR makes the vsim ROI run cached. `cache_off.elf` (same `main.c`, `-DCACHE_OFF`) clears IC_EN|DC_EN before the ROI, so the transported value disables the caches — showing what every hybrid figure would look like without the transport. `check.sh` asserts both fast builds print `CACHE_OK` and that uncached > 2x cached (`RATIO_MIN` overridable); its teeth were verified with `RATIO_MIN=99`, which fails with exit 1 as it should. There is deliberately no `cache-off-cycle` target: disabling the D-cache mid-run on the RTL would strand dirty lines, while on hybrid the vsim caches start empty so the plain disable is exact.

One real finding from the way there: the first kernel (16 passes x 4 KB) made the uncached vsim leg exceed the driver's per-leg timeout — the repro bundle's manifest pinned it to step 1, the accurate leg, and the 90 s value is a fixed default in `driver/run_plan.hpp:92` with no CLI or env override. I resized the kernel to 4 passes x 256 words (uncached leg now ~16 s) and documented the sizing constraint in `main.c`. If you ever want uncached CoreMark-scale windows, that timeout will need a knob in andesim.

Remaining figures: cycle mode 16,790 cycles from reset; hybrid-pc 4,541 agrees with marker's 4,544. ROADMAP now has fp and cache DONE; next up per the roadmap: `hotloops`, `verify`, `kanata`.

# andesim-demo test roadmap

Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.

Conventions (same as the existing demos):

- Layout: `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; host-side checks go
  in `demo/<name>/check.sh` (the `memsize` precedent).
- Top-level `Makefile` gets `run-<name>` and the per-mode targets; `README.md`
  gets a short section describing what the demo proves.
- Pass signal: either the guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI, or
  `check.sh` asserts on the driver's output. Every demo must fail loudly.
- Demos run on every mode where the feature exists (some are hybrid-only or
  fast-only; each entry says which).

Priority = file order. 1-3 are headline USER_GUIDE features with zero demo
coverage today.

---

## 1. hotloops

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (pc trigger); the detector itself runs fast.

Measure a binary you cannot edit. `main.c` has one known hot loop (a
checksum over an array, >=10 iterations) and NO ROI markers. `check.sh`
runs `$(ANDESIM)/build/hotloops --min-iters 10 <elf>`, asserts the report
names the hot function, extracts the ready `measure:` line (a
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair), and pastes it into
`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`. Closed loop: the detector's
output feeds the measurement command with no human guessing.

- Key files: `demo/hotloops/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh sees the hot function in the hotloops report AND a
  `[andesim] N cycles` line from the hybrid run using the reported PCs.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 4.3, docs/hotloops.md.

## 2. verify

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid only (marker trigger).

Trust the figure. A state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP math, an RVV
loop, CSR writes) runs with `--verify`: andesim re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU
up to the ROI exit and compares the drained state field by field against
the cycle engine.

- Key files: `demo/verify/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: output contains `[state-diff] PASS` and `[verify] PASS: vsim drain
  matches the QEMU oracle`.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.7.

## 3. kanata

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid only.

See the pipeline of exactly the ROI. A small kernel runs with
`--kanata roi.kanata --objdump kernel.S` (the dump generated at build time
with `objdump -d`). Users open the file in Konata; check.sh proves it is
well-formed without a GUI.

- Key files: `demo/kanata/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts the Kanata header line, that a known kernel
  mnemonic from the objdump is embedded, and the trace is non-trivial
  (more than a handful of retired instructions).
- Constraint to demo: marker mode needs exactly ONE exit marker in the ELF
  (more -> andesim errors and points at `--trigger pc`).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.8.

## 4. engines

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (optionally cycle too) on BOTH installed engines.

One binary, N cores - design-space exploration. The same kernel is measured
on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` and `vsim:ax46mpv_advanced`; check.sh parses both
cycle figures and prints a small comparison table.

- Key files: `demo/engines/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: both engines produce a `[andesim] N cycles` line; table printed.
- Deps: none. Requires both engines installed (skip with a clear message if
  `list engines` shows only one).

## 5. fp

State: DONE
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).

Scalar FP state transport - fills the coverage gap next to `rvv` (which is
integer-V only). The QEMU phase sets a non-default rounding mode (`frm` =
RTZ) and raises a sticky `fflags` bit; the vsim ROI computes a
rounding-mode-sensitive result and checks: the result matches
expected-for-RTZ, and the pre-ROI sticky flag is still set. Proves
`fcsr` (+ `mstatus.FS`) crossed the handoff.

- Key files: `demo/fp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest prints `FP_OK`.
- Deps: none.

## 6. cache

State: DONE
Modes: hybrid (marker), two variants of one source.

Why timing-config transport matters. The same kernel is built twice from
one `main.c`: variant A keeps crt0's cache enable (transported
`mcache_ctl`), variant B writes `mcache_ctl = 0` before the ROI. check.sh
runs both hybrid measurements and asserts the uncached figure is much
larger. Doubles as a write-mask demo: the restore carries variant B's
disable only because the program itself wrote the CSR.

- Key files: `demo/cache/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(off) > 2 * cycles(on)` (calibrate the
  factor once real numbers exist).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE section 6 ("Config that matters for
  timing rides along").

## 7. roi_rules

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (marker + pc) vs cycle as the reference.

Trigger semantics and measurement hygiene, executable. A `noinline` kernel
is called 3 times; both triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is
the FIRST call only. check.sh asserts the hybrid figure is far below the
cycle-mode total (which contains all 3 calls + boot). The source shows the
hygiene rule from USER_GUIDE 4.2: anchor the kernel through memory inside
the marker span.

- Key files: `demo/roi_rules/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(hybrid) < cycles(cycle) / 3`.
- Deps: none.

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (driver features, no new guest code needed - reuse the hello ELF).

The debugging workflow as a script. check.sh exercises, in order:
`--dry-run` (asserts 2 resolved command lines), `--print-memmap` (asserts
the DRAM/V-scratch rows), `--log-level 1` (asserts the `[andesim] mmap`
line), `--log-file` (asserts timestamped, level-tagged lines land in the
file), and one forced leg failure that must leave a repro bundle
(`[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at ...` -> assert `manifest.txt`
exists there). Open point for the build session: pick the most reliable
quick failure (candidate: a `--pc-end` that never retires, with a short

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-rvv
make run-fp
make run-cache
make run-syscall
make run-coremark
make run-dhrystone
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `fp-*`, `cache-*`, `syscall-*`,
`coremark-*` and `dhrystone-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/rvv` tests the vector unit: the ROI runs an RVV-intrinsic kernel
(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works); the
workload is an 8x8x8 int32 GEMM. The QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar
reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector unit and
compares. `RVV_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after the
handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

`demo/fp` covers the scalar FPU's state, `fcsr`, the way `demo/rvv`
covers the vector unit. The QEMU phase clears `fflags`, sets the
rounding mode to RTZ (the reset default is RNE) and raises the sticky
divide-by-zero flag with a real `1.0f/0.0f`; the vsim ROI computes
`1.0f/3.0f` -- a quotient that rounds DIFFERENTLY under RTZ
(`0x3eaaaaaa`) and RNE (`0x3eaaaaab`) -- then reads the CSRs back.
`FP_OK` means the transported `frm` steered a real divide after the
handoff (not just a CSR readback), the pre-handoff DZ flag is still
sticky, and the divide's own NX landed on top of it: `fcsr` crossed
intact.

`demo/cache` prices the config transport: the SAME kernel (4 passes
over a 1 KB volatile array) in two hybrid builds. `cache_on` is the
untouched program -- crt0 enables the L1 caches at boot, and only the
transported `mcache_ctl` makes the vsim ROI run cached, as this
program would on silicon. `cache_off` clears the IC|DC enable bits
before the ROI, so the transported value disables the caches and the
same window runs uncached -- about 4.5k vs 42.5k cycles, a ~9x gap on
this kernel (`make check-cache` asserts ratio > 2x). Without the
transport EVERY hybrid figure would look like `cache_off`: the engine
resets with caches off. There is no cache_off cycle target on
purpose: disabling the D-cache mid-run on the RTL would strand its
dirty lines (that needs a CCTL flush first); on hybrid the vsim
caches start empty at the restore, so the plain disable is exact.

`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
main's return value through SimControl).

`demo/coremark` runs a real benchmark, EEMBC CoreMark, with the EEMBC
sources untouched: the ROI markers live in the port layer
(`core_portme.c`), inside `start_time()` and `stop_time()` -- the two
functions that already delimit the timed run -- so the hybrid window is
exactly the region CoreMark times itself with its own `mcycle` reads.
That makes the modes cross-check each other: cycle mode's self-reported
`Total ticks` and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region and agree within ~0.5% (the hybrid window starts with cold
caches and includes the marker/call boundary). The pc-trigger variant
gets the same window from the symbols alone
(`--pc-start start_time --pc-end stop_time`). On hybrid the run ends at
`stop_time()`'s exit marker, so CoreMark's report (CRCs, validation)
prints on fast and cycle only; the hybrid output is just the cycle
figure. `ITERATIONS=1` by default -- the CRCs still validate, and each
extra iteration adds RTL simulation time.

`demo/dhrystone` applies the same recipe to Dhrystone 2.2a (the vsim
port, which times with `mcycle`/`minstret` instead of UNIX time APIs):
the counter reads moved into `start_time()`/`stop_time()`, which carry
the ROI markers outside the reads and double as the
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbols. The guest's self-reported `CycleCnt`
(cycle mode) and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region; on hybrid the run ends at `stop_time()`'s marker, so the
`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
second pass with `-DPASS2`).

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/rvv/       RVV-intrinsic kernel (8x8x8 GEMM) inside the ROI
demo/fp/        scalar FP state: frm steers a divide in the ROI, fflags stay sticky
demo/cache/     the mcache_ctl transport, priced: one kernel cached vs uncached
demo/syscall/   stdio, host file io and exit code on every mode
demo/coremark/  EEMBC CoreMark; the ROI is the benchmark's own timed region
demo/dhrystone/ Dhrystone 2.2a; same recipe, two-pass compile kept
```

# Shared configuration
-include Make.var

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/rvv demo/fp demo/cache \
           demo/syscall demo/coremark demo/dhrystone demo/memsize

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run check clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

hvm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_dma $@

rvv-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/rvv $@

fp-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/fp $@

cache-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/cache $@

syscall-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/syscall $@

coremark-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/coremark $@

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

memsize-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/memsize $@

# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
check:
	@fail=""; \
	for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
	  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
	    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
	  else \
	    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "===================================="; \
	if [ -z "$$fail" ]; then echo "ALL DEMOS OK"; \
	else echo "FAILED DEMOS:$$fail"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:
	@if $(MAKE) -C demo/$* -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* check; \
	else \
	  echo "demo/$*: no asserts -- running to assert exit 0"; \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* run; \
	fi

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-asserting harness for the cache demo: the transported cache-enable
# state must be worth a multiple in the hybrid cycle figure. Same pattern as
# demo/memsize/check.sh.
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
ENG=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}
RATIO_MIN=${RATIO_MIN:-2}   # uncached must cost > RATIO_MIN x cached

pass=0 fail=0
# assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD...
assert() {
  local desc=$1 want_rc=$2 want_re=$3; shift 3
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] && grep -qiE "$want_re" <<<"$out"; then
    printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$desc"; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] %s\n       rc=%s (want %s), no /%s/ in:\n       %s\n' \
      "$desc" "$rc" "$want_rc" "$want_re" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

# run_cycles CMD... -> echoes the N of "[andesim] N cycles", empty on failure
run_cycles() {
  local out
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1) || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; return 1; }
  sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1
}

    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] uncached/cached ratio %sx did not clear %sx\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Design-space sweep: measure the SAME ELF on every installed vsim engine
# and print the comparison table. The engine set comes from
# `andesim list engines` at run time (rows with TYPE vsim and an XLEN
# matching this rv64 ELF) -- nothing is hardcoded. Override with
# ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b" to restrict the sweep. Same assert pattern as
# demo/memsize/check.sh.
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}

pass=0 fail=0
# assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD...
assert() {
  local desc=$1 want_rc=$2 want_re=$3; shift 3
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] && grep -qiE "$want_re" <<<"$out"; then
    printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$desc"; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] %s\n       rc=%s (want %s), no /%s/ in:\n       %s\n' \
      "$desc" "$rc" "$want_rc" "$want_re" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

# run_cycles CMD... -> echoes the N of "[andesim] N cycles", empty on failure
run_cycles() {
  local out
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1) || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; return 1; }
  sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1
}

# All vsim engines the driver can run this rv64 ELF on.
list_vsim_engines() {
  "$A" list engines </dev/null 2>/dev/null |
    awk '$2 == "vsim" && $4 == 64 { print $1 }'
}

ENGINES=${ENGINES:-$(list_vsim_engines | tr '\n' ' ')}

if [ -z "${ENGINES// /}" ]; then
  echo "[SKIP] no rv64 vsim engine installed (see: andesim list engines)"
  exit 0
fi

echo "--- the one binary is functionally sound (fast) ---"
assert "fast: ENGINES_OK" 0 "ENGINES_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast engines.elf

echo "--- the same ROI, hybrid, on every vsim engine ---"
names=() cycles=()
for eng in $ENGINES; do
  cyc=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$eng" engines.elf)
  if [ -n "$cyc" ]; then
    printf '[PASS] %-24s %8s cycles\n' "$eng" "$cyc"; pass=$((pass+1))
    names+=("$eng"); cycles+=("$cyc")
  else
    printf '[FAIL] %-24s no "[andesim] N cycles" line\n' "$eng"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
done

if [ "${#names[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  best=${cycles[0]}
  for c in "${cycles[@]}"; do [ "$c" -lt "$best" ] && best=$c; done
  echo
  printf '%-24s %10s %9s\n' "ENGINE" "CYCLES" "vs best"
  for i in "${!names[@]}"; do
    printf '%-24s %10s %9s\n' "${names[$i]}" "${cycles[$i]}" \
      "$(awk -v c="${cycles[$i]}" -v b="$best" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2fx", c/b}')"
  done
  [ "${#names[@]}" -lt 2 ] && \
    echo "note: only one vsim engine installed -- nothing to compare against"
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

content.content:
usage: andesim [command] [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]

Multi-engine driver for the Andes simulators (QEMU + vsim).

run     run one simulation (the default: 'run' may be omitted)
  fast      QEMU only -- functional, full speed
  cycle     one cycle-accurate engine, from reset
  hybrid    QEMU fast-forwards, then vsim measures the ROI

  --mode fast|cycle|hybrid    REQUIRED  which mode to run
  --trigger marker|pc         REQUIRED for hybrid  the ROI delimiter
    --pc-start <sym|0x>       REQUIRED for --trigger pc  ROI start boundary
    --pc-end <sym|0x>         REQUIRED for --trigger pc  ROI end boundary
  --engine <id>               pick an engine, e.g. vsim:ax45mpv_premium (default: the sole one)
  --mem-size <spec>           guest RAM, e.g. 256M / 2G (hybrid: max 2G; fast: QEMU -m; cycle: ignored)
  --dry-run                   print the exact engine command(s) and exit, running nothing (fast/cycle/hybrid)
  --print-memmap              print the hybrid guest memory map and exit, running nothing (hybrid only; ELF optional)
  --verify                    cross-check the hybrid run against a QEMU oracle
  --kanata <file>             write a Kanata pipeline trace of the ROI (hybrid only; open in Konata)
    --objdump <file>          embed that objdump -d dump's disassembly in the trace (requires --kanata)
  --gdb                       pause at startup for a debugger (fast: QEMU stub; cycle: vsim JTAG + $ICEMAN; not hybrid)
  --gdb-port <port>           override the --gdb port (fast 1234, cycle 9104)
  --log-level <0-6>           verbosity, vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off (default 2: program output + the cycle figure)
  --log-file <file>           append EVERY level's messages (timestamped) to <file>; the console keeps --log-level
  -- <args...>                forward everything after -- verbatim to the engine (fast/cycle only; hybrid rejects -- args)

list    list what is available
  models    the modes and their engines
  engines   discovered cycle-accurate engines

doctor  check toolchain + fixtures are present

'andesim run --help' / 'andesim list --help' for per-command detail.
----
list    list what is available
  models    the modes and their engines
  engines   discovered cycle-accurate engines

# Shared configuration
-include Make.var

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/rvv demo/fp demo/cache \
           demo/syscall demo/coremark demo/dhrystone demo/memsize

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run check clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

hvm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_dma $@

rvv-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/rvv $@

fp-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/fp $@

cache-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/cache $@

syscall-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/syscall $@

coremark-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/coremark $@

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

memsize-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/memsize $@

# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
check:
	@fail=""; \
	for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
	  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
	    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
	  else \
	    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "===================================="; \
	if [ -z "$$fail" ]; then echo "ALL DEMOS OK"; \
	else echo "FAILED DEMOS:$$fail"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:
	@if $(MAKE) -C demo/$* -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* check; \
	else \
	  echo "demo/$*: no asserts -- running to assert exit 0"; \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* run; \
	fi

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

# ---- Engine sweep --------------------------------------------------------
# Demos that need hardware not every engine has. The sweep skips them on an
# engine whose resolved hybrid plan (--dry-run) carries no ILM/DLM/HVM
# sidecar args, or whose `list engines` row shows no VLEN.
NEED_LM  := demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma
NEED_HVM := demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma
NEED_V   := demo/rvv

# Run the aggregate `check` once per installed vsim engine -- the engine set
# is parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (rv64 rows; the demos
# are rv64 builds). Restrict it with SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b". Fails if
# any engine fails any demo it is capable of.
check-all-engines:
	@engines="$(SWEEP_ENGINES)"; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  engines=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	             | awk '$$2 == "vsim" && $$4 == 64 { print $$1 }'); \
	fi; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  echo "no rv64 vsim engine installed (see: andesim list engines)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello hello.elf >/dev/null; \
	summary=""; bad=""; \
	for eng in $$engines; do \
	  plan=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
	          --engine "$$eng" --dry-run demo/hello/hello.elf </dev/null 2>&1); \
	  vlen=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	          | awk -v e="$$eng" '$$1 == e { print $$5 }'); \
	  skips=""; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "ilm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_LM)"; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "hvm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_HVM)"; \
	  case "$$vlen" in ""|-|0) skips="$$skips $(NEED_V)";; esac; \
	  dirs=""; \
	  for d in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	    case " $$skips " in *" $$d "*) ;; *) dirs="$$dirs $$d";; esac; \
	  done; \
	  echo "#################### ENGINE $$eng ####################"; \
	  if [ -n "$$skips" ]; then echo "[SKIP] $$eng lacks the hardware for:$$skips"; fi; \
	  if $(MAKE) check ENGINE="$$eng" SUBDIRS="$$dirs"; then \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: OK (skipped:$${skips:- none})"; \
	  else \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: FAILED"; bad="$$bad $$eng"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "#################### ENGINE SWEEP ####################"; \
	printf "engines:$$summary\n"; \
	if [ -n "$$bad" ]; then echo "FAILED ENGINES:$$bad"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:

	$(MAKE) -C demo/fp $@

syscall-%:

coremark-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/coremark $@

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

memsize-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/memsize $@

# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
check:
	@fail=""; \
	for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
	  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
	    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
	  else \
	    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "===================================="; \
	if [ -z "$$fail" ]; then echo "ALL DEMOS OK"; \
	else echo "FAILED DEMOS:$$fail"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:
	@if $(MAKE) -C demo/$* -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* check; \
	else \
	  echo "demo/$*: no asserts -- running to assert exit 0"; \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* run; \
	fi

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

## Switching engines

Every `cycle` and `hybrid` target takes its engine from the `ENGINE`
variable (default in `Make.var`), so any demo runs on any engine that

at run time (nothing hardcoded; restrict it with

(`lm*`, `hvm*`) are skipped on an engine whose resolved plan carries
no ILM/DLM/HVM (e.g. `ax46mpv_advanced` has none), and `rvv` is
skipped on an engine without a vector unit.

# andesim-demo test roadmap

Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.

Conventions (same as the existing demos):

- Layout: `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; host-side checks go
  in `demo/<name>/check.sh` (the `memsize` precedent).
- Top-level `Makefile` gets `run-<name>` and the per-mode targets; `README.md`
  gets a short section describing what the demo proves.
- Pass signal: either the guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI, or
  `check.sh` asserts on the driver's output. Every demo must fail loudly.
- Demos run on every mode where the feature exists (some are hybrid-only or
  fast-only; each entry says which).

Priority = file order. 1-3 are headline USER_GUIDE features with zero demo
coverage today.

---

## 1. hotloops

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (pc trigger); the detector itself runs fast.

Measure a binary you cannot edit. `main.c` has one known hot loop (a
checksum over an array, >=10 iterations) and NO ROI markers. `check.sh`
runs `$(ANDESIM)/build/hotloops --min-iters 10 <elf>`, asserts the report
names the hot function, extracts the ready `measure:` line (a
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair), and pastes it into
`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`. Closed loop: the detector's
output feeds the measurement command with no human guessing.

- Key files: `demo/hotloops/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh sees the hot function in the hotloops report AND a
  `[andesim] N cycles` line from the hybrid run using the reported PCs.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 4.3, docs/hotloops.md.

## 2. verify

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid only (marker trigger).

Trust the figure. A state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP math, an RVV
loop, CSR writes) runs with `--verify`: andesim re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU
up to the ROI exit and compares the drained state field by field against
the cycle engine.

- Key files: `demo/verify/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: output contains `[state-diff] PASS` and `[verify] PASS: vsim drain
  matches the QEMU oracle`.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.7.

## 3. kanata

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid only.

See the pipeline of exactly the ROI. A small kernel runs with
`--kanata roi.kanata --objdump kernel.S` (the dump generated at build time
with `objdump -d`). Users open the file in Konata; check.sh proves it is
well-formed without a GUI.

- Key files: `demo/kanata/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts the Kanata header line, that a known kernel
  mnemonic from the objdump is embedded, and the trace is non-trivial
  (more than a handful of retired instructions).
- Constraint to demo: marker mode needs exactly ONE exit marker in the ELF
  (more -> andesim errors and points at `--trigger pc`).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.8.

## 4. engines

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (optionally cycle too) on BOTH installed engines.

One binary, N cores - design-space exploration. The same kernel is measured
on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` and `vsim:ax46mpv_advanced`; check.sh parses both
cycle figures and prints a small comparison table.

- Key files: `demo/engines/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: both engines produce a `[andesim] N cycles` line; table printed.
- Deps: none. Requires both engines installed (skip with a clear message if
  `list engines` shows only one).

## 5. fp

State: DONE
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).

Scalar FP state transport - fills the coverage gap next to `rvv` (which is
integer-V only). The QEMU phase sets a non-default rounding mode (`frm` =
RTZ) and raises a sticky `fflags` bit; the vsim ROI computes a
rounding-mode-sensitive result and checks: the result matches
expected-for-RTZ, and the pre-ROI sticky flag is still set. Proves
`fcsr` (+ `mstatus.FS`) crossed the handoff.

- Key files: `demo/fp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest prints `FP_OK`.
- Deps: none.

## 6. cache

State: DONE
Modes: hybrid (marker), two variants of one source.

Why timing-config transport matters. The same kernel is built twice from
one `main.c`: variant A keeps crt0's cache enable (transported
`mcache_ctl`), variant B writes `mcache_ctl = 0` before the ROI. check.sh
runs both hybrid measurements and asserts the uncached figure is much
larger. Doubles as a write-mask demo: the restore carries variant B's
disable only because the program itself wrote the CSR.

- Key files: `demo/cache/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(off) > 2 * cycles(on)` (calibrate the
  factor once real numbers exist).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE section 6 ("Config that matters for
  timing rides along").

## 7. roi_rules

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (marker + pc) vs cycle as the reference.

Trigger semantics and measurement hygiene, executable. A `noinline` kernel
is called 3 times; both triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is
the FIRST call only. check.sh asserts the hybrid figure is far below the
cycle-mode total (which contains all 3 calls + boot). The source shows the
hygiene rule from USER_GUIDE 4.2: anchor the kernel through memory inside
the marker span.

- Key files: `demo/roi_rules/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(hybrid) < cycles(cycle) / 3`.
- Deps: none.

## 8. diagnose

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (driver features, no new guest code needed - reuse the hello ELF).

The debugging workflow as a script. check.sh exercises, in order:
`--dry-run` (asserts 2 resolved command lines), `--print-memmap` (asserts
the DRAM/V-scratch rows), `--log-level 1` (asserts the `[andesim] mmap`
line), `--log-file` (asserts timestamped, level-tagged lines land in the
file), and one forced leg failure that must leave a repro bundle
(`[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at ...` -> assert `manifest.txt`
exists there). Open point for the build session: pick the most reliable
quick failure (candidate: a `--pc-end` that never retires, with a short
timeout).

- Key files: `demo/diagnose/{Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: every assertion in check.sh.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.5, 5.6, 5.10, 8.

## 9. rv32

State: TODO
Modes: fast only (no rv32 cycle engine installed; hybrid rejects rv32 by design).

The rv32 runtime flavor and engine auto-select. Build hello against
`build/runtime/rv32` (`-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d`), run `--mode fast` with
no `--engine`, and show the driver picked `qemu32` from the ELF width.

- Key files: `demo/rv32/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: hello output + exit code propagated; `--log-level 1` (or
  `--dry-run`) shows qemu32 was selected.
- Deps: needs an rv32-capable compiler (separate riscv32 gcc or multilib);
  the Makefile must skip with a clear message if the toolchain cannot do
  rv32.

## 10. gdb

State: TODO
Modes: fast first; cycle as a stretch goal.

Attach a debugger, scripted. fast: launch `--gdb` in the background, drive
`gdb-multiarch` in batch mode (`-ex 'target remote :1234'`, break at a

2. Key Technical Concepts:
